description: Hormonal treatment options for menopause symptoms

entries.title: Hormone Replacement Therapy (HRT) Overview
entries.description: The main medical treatment for menopause symptoms using hormones to replace declining levels
entries.content: Hormone Replacement Therapy (HRT), also called Hormone Therapy (HT), is the most effective treatment for menopausal symptoms, particularly hot flashes, night sweats, vaginal dryness, and mood symptoms. HRT replaces estrogen (and progesterone if you have a uterus) that the body no longer produces at sufficient levels. It can reduce hot flashes by 75-90%, improve sleep quality, enhance mood, prevent bone loss, and improve overall quality of life during menopause.
entries.effectiveness: Highly effective - reduces hot flashes by 75-90%, most effective treatment available
entries.who_can_use: Most women going through menopause, especially those under 60 or within 10 years of menopause onset
who_should_avoid: History of blood clots or stroke
benefits: Relieves hot flashes and night sweats (75-90% reduction)
Improves vaginal dryness and urinary symptoms
Reduces joint pain and muscle aches
Improves mood, brain fog, and sleep
Prevents osteoporosis and reduces fracture risk
May reduce cardiovascular disease risk when started early
risks: Small increased risk of breast cancer with long-term combined HRT (estrogen + progestin)
Small increased risk of blood clots (especially with oral estrogen)
Small increased risk of stroke in older women
Risks are generally small and outweighed by benefits for most women
important_notes: Safest and most beneficial when started before age 60 or within 10 years of menopause
Risks vary based on type, dose, duration, and individual factors
Regular follow-up with healthcare provider recommended
Can be taken as long as benefits outweigh risks
entries.when_to_see_doctor: Discuss HRT with your doctor if menopausal symptoms are affecting your quality of life

entries.title: Estrogen Therapy (ET)
entries.description: Estrogen-only hormone therapy for women without a uterus
entries.content: Estrogen Therapy (ET) involves taking estrogen alone without progesterone. This is only appropriate for women who have had a hysterectomy (uterus removed), as estrogen alone can cause uterine lining overgrowth and increase cancer risk in women with a uterus. ET is highly effective for menopausal symptoms and comes in various forms.
forms: Gels or sprays applied to skin daily
entries.dosing: Lowest effective dose for symptom relief
entries.effectiveness: Highly effective for all menopausal symptoms
benefits: Relieves vasomotor symptoms (hot flashes, night sweats)
May have lower breast cancer risk than combined therapy
entries.preferred_forms: Transdermal (patches, gels) preferred over oral for lower blood clot risk
entries.when_to_see_doctor: Discuss with doctor to determine appropriate type and dose

entries.title: Combined Hormone Therapy (EPT)
entries.description: Estrogen plus progesterone therapy for women with a uterus
entries.content: Combined Hormone Therapy (EPT), also called Estrogen-Progestogen Therapy, uses both estrogen and progesterone (or progestin, a synthetic form). The progesterone is essential for women with a uterus to protect the uterine lining from overgrowth and cancer risk caused by estrogen alone. EPT is highly effective for menopausal symptoms.
entries.who_must_use: Any woman with a uterus taking systemic estrogen MUST also take progesterone
regimens: Continuous combined: Daily estrogen + daily progesterone (no periods)
Sequential/cyclical: Daily estrogen + progesterone for part of month (may have withdrawal bleeding)
considerations: Slightly higher breast cancer risk than estrogen alone with long-term use
Risk is still small and depends on duration and type of progestin
Benefits often outweigh risks, especially when started early
entries.when_to_see_doctor: Required for women with uterus taking estrogen

entries.title: Vaginal Estrogen
entries.description: Low-dose estrogen applied directly to the vagina for local symptoms
entries.content: Vaginal estrogen is a low-dose estrogen treatment applied directly to the vagina to treat vaginal dryness, atrophy, pain during sex, and urinary symptoms. Unlike systemic HRT, vaginal estrogen works locally with minimal absorption into the bloodstream, making it very safe for long-term use. It can be used alone or alongside systemic HRT.
forms: Vaginal rings (inserted and changed every 3 months)
entries.who_can_use: Most women with vaginal/urinary symptoms, including many who cannot use systemic HRT
entries.effectiveness: Highly effective for vaginal dryness, pain during sex, and urinary symptoms
benefits: Improves urinary symptoms and reduces UTI risk
Can be used with systemic HRT
entries.duration: Can be used for life; symptoms typically return if stopped
entries.safety: Very safe, even for women who cannot use systemic HRT
entries.when_to_see_doctor: Discuss if experiencing vaginal dryness or urinary symptoms

entries.title: Testosterone Therapy
entries.description: Testosterone gel or cream for low libido in menopausal women
entries.content: Testosterone therapy can help restore sex drive (libido) in menopausal women when HRT alone doesn't help. Testosterone is produced by the ovaries and levels decline with age. While not officially licensed for women in many countries, it can be prescribed off-label by specialists. It's safe to use alongside HRT.
entries.who_can_use: Women with low libido not improved by HRT, prescribed by specialist
entries.effectiveness: Can improve libido, mood, and energy in some women
side_effects: Can affect others if they contact treated skin - wash hands after use and cover area
entries.safety: Generally safe when properly dosed and monitored
entries.when_to_see_doctor: Discuss with specialist if low libido persists despite HRT

entries.title: Bioidentical Hormones (Body-Identical Hormones)
entries.description: Hormones chemically identical to those the body produces
entries.content: Bioidentical or body-identical hormones are hormones that are chemically identical to those produced by the human body. Many regulated HRT products available on the NHS and by prescription are bioidentical, including micronized progesterone and 17-beta estradiol. These are different from compounded bioidentical hormones, which are custom-mixed and not regulated. Regulated bioidentical hormones are safe, tested, and effective.
benefits: May have better side effect profile for some women
Micronized progesterone may have lower breast cancer and blood clot risk than synthetic progestins
entries.important_distinction: Regulated bioidentical hormones (available by prescription) are different from unregulated compounded bioidentical hormones (not recommended)
entries.when_to_see_doctor: Discuss bioidentical options with your doctor

entries.title: Prasterone (Intrarosa)
entries.description: DHEA vaginal insert for vaginal dryness
entries.content: Prasterone is a vaginal insert containing DHEA (dehydroepiandrosterone), a hormone that the body converts to estrogen and testosterone locally in vaginal tissues. It's used to treat vaginal dryness and pain during intercourse in postmenopausal women.
entries.effectiveness: Effective for vaginal dryness and painful intercourse
benefits: Works locally with minimal systemic absorption

entries.title: HRT Duration and Follow-up
entries.description: How long to take HRT and monitoring recommendations
entries.content: There is no arbitrary time limit for HRT. Women can take HRT as long as the benefits outweigh the risks for their individual situation. Many women take HRT for several years; some continue for decades. Regular follow-up with a healthcare provider is important to reassess benefits, risks, and appropriateness.
entries.ongoing_reviews: Annually, or more often if needed
what_happens_at_reviews: Check for side effects or vaginal bleeding
Review type and dose of HRT
duration_guidance: Can continue as long as benefits outweigh risks
Symptoms often return if HRT is stopped
Can restart HRT if needed after stopping
